S025.name: Loss_of_Interest
S025.description: A state where interest or pleasure in previously enjoyed activities is markedly diminished.

subtypes.Loss of Interest: Reduced interest in previously enjoyed hobbies or leisure activities.
subtypes.Social Withdrawal: Reduced interest or effort in social interactions and maintaining relationships.
subtypes.Loss of Motivation: Lack of motivation to initiate or complete work or tasks.
subtypes.Anhedonia: Inability to experience positive emotions such as happiness, satisfaction, love, or pleasure.
subtypes.Indifference to Achievement: Insensitivity or indifference to personal achievements or success.

S026.name: Weight_Appetite_Change
S026.description: Significant increase or decrease in appetite or weight.

subtypes.Significant Weight Loss: Weight loss of more than 5% in a month without dieting.
subtypes.Weight Gain: Weight gain of more than 5% in a month.
subtypes.Decrease in Appetite: Decrease in appetite occurring nearly every day.
subtypes.Increase in Appetite: Increase in appetite occurring nearly every day.

S027.name: Sleep_Disturbance
S027.description: A state where there is a significant change in the quantity or quality of sleep.

subtypes.Initial Insomnia: Difficulty falling asleep and taking a long time to do so.
subtypes.Middle Insomnia: Waking up frequently during sleep or having difficulty falling back asleep.
subtypes.Early Morning Awakening: Waking up too early and being unable to fall back asleep.
subtypes.Hypersomnia: Sleeping for long periods at night or excessive sleep during the day.
subtypes.Nightmare Disorder: Sleep disturbance caused by repeated and distressing dreams.
subtypes.Non-Restorative Sleep: Feeling unrefreshed despite having slept enough.

S029.name: Fatigue
S029.description: Persistent fatigue that is not relieved by rest and a marked lack of energy.

subtypes.Chronic Fatigue: Fatigue that persists for a long period even after adequate rest.
subtypes.Physical Fatigue: A state of physical exhaustion where the body feels heavy and easily tires even from minor activities.
subtypes.Mental Fatigue: A state where fatigue accumulates rapidly during the process of thinking or concentrating.
subtypes.Loss of Energy: Difficulty performing daily activities due to a decline in energy and vitality.

S030.name: Worthlessness_Guilt
S030.description: Feelings of worthlessness or excessive or inappropriate guilt (which may be delusional; not merely self-reproach or guilt about being sick).

subtypes.Feelings of Worthlessness: The feeling that one is useless and has no value.
subtypes.Ruminative Guilt: A thought pattern of obsessively replaying past minor mistakes or flaws and constantly reproaching oneself.
subtypes.Excessive or Inappropriate Guilt: Feeling excessive responsibility for trivial matters or daily events and believing one deserves punishment.
subtypes.Delusional Guilt: Guilt reaching a delusional level, disconnected from reality, involving feeling responsible for unrelated unfortunate events.

S031.name: Diminished_Thinking
S031.description: Diminished ability to think or concentrate, or indecisiveness.

subtypes.Reduced Concentration: Unable to pay attention or maintain focus on specific activities like conversation, reading, or watching TV.
subtypes.Indecisiveness: Extreme difficulty making even minor daily choices (e.g., menu, clothes) and hesitating to make decisions.
subtypes.Subjective Memory Complaints: Complaining of memory decline, such as forgetting where things were placed, due to reduced focus.
subtypes.Clouded Thinking: Thinking feels foggy, dazed, or not clear.

S032.name: Death_Suicide
S032.description: Recurrent thoughts of death, recurrent suicidal ideation, or a suicide attempt.

subtypes.Recurrent Thoughts of Death: Passive wish to die (e.g., 'I wish I wouldn't wake up') without active intent to kill oneself.
subtypes.Suicidal Ideation: Recurring thoughts of 'I want to die' or 'I want to kill myself' without a specific plan.
subtypes.Suicidal Impulse: Strong, sudden urges to jump from a height or run into traffic without a concrete plan.
subtypes.Specific Plan for Suicide: Conceiving specific scenarios or methods regarding when, where, and how to die.
subtypes.Suicide Attempt: Actual actions taken to end one's life or preparatory behaviors like hoarding pills or writing a will.

symptom.disease_info: Major Depressive Disorder (MDD) is characterized by one or more major depressive episodes lasting at least two weeks, involving a persistent low mood or loss of interest along with associated cognitive, somatic, and behavioral changes that cause clinically significant distress or impairment. Typical features include changes in sleep, appetite or weight, energy, concentration, self-worth, and recurrent thoughts of death or suicide. The course can be single-episode or recurrent, with episodes often triggered by psychosocial stressors, medical illness, or occurring without clear precipitant, and may become chronic if untreated. MDD is distinguished from bipolar disorders by the absence of manic or hypomanic episodes and from normal grief by its pervasive impairment, self-critical or hopeless ruminations, and loss of capacity for pleasure that extends beyond culturally expected bereavement reactions.

patient.personality: Mario is a quiet, meticulous, and thrifty man who finds comfort in routine, gardening, and solitary pastimes while remaining quietly devoted to his close-knit neighborhood.
patient.stressor: Roughly two years ago, Mario underwent surgery and was diagnosed with a chronic cardiac condition that forced him to give up most of his handyman work and cut back on his long walks in Griffith Park. This health setback, coming on the heels of several years of widowhood, disrupted the carefully structured routines that had helped him feel useful and in control, and it left him increasingly preoccupied with his physical limitations and the fear of further decline. Over time he began spending more evenings alone at his kitchen table, poring over his expense ledger and worrying about becoming dependent on his children, while his once restorative gardening and neighborhood repairs felt more like exhausting obligations than sources of pride. As he grew more worn down and his nights became increasingly fragmented with long hours awake, his daughter urged him to seek psychiatric help after he admitted that he dreaded going to bed because he could no longer get a solid night’s sleep and felt he was “falling apart” without understanding why.
patient.chief_complaint: “I just can’t sleep through the night anymore, no matter how tired I am.”

S025.name: Loss_of_Interest
S025.description: A state where interest or pleasure in previously enjoyed activities is markedly diminished.
S025.manifestation: I used to fuss over my roses and help the neighbors fix little things around their houses, but these days I mostly just sit at the kitchen table staring at the garden, feeling like I can’t be bothered to get up and do any of it because nothing really feels good anymore.

S026.name: Weight_Appetite_Change
S026.description: Significant increase or decrease in appetite or weight.
S026.manifestation: Ever since my heart trouble, food just doesn’t appeal to me much—most days I pick at half a sandwich or some crackers, and my daughter keeps telling me my pants look looser but I just don’t feel hungry.

S027.name: Sleep_Disturbance
S027.description: A state where there is a significant change in the quantity or quality of sleep.
S027.manifestation: When I go to bed, I fall asleep for an hour or two and then I’m wide awake, tossing and turning, watching the clock crawl through the night and getting up to sit in the dark kitchen because I know I’m not going back to sleep properly.

S029.name: Fatigue
S029.description: Persistent fatigue that is not relieved by rest and a marked lack of energy.
S029.manifestation: Even on days when I don’t do much of anything, I feel worn out, like my body is made of lead, and just sweeping the patio or walking to the corner makes me want to sit down and rest right away.

S030.name: Worthlessness_Guilt
S030.description: Feelings of worthlessness or excessive or inappropriate guilt (which may be delusional; not merely self-reproach or guilt about being sick).
S030.manifestation: I keep thinking I’m a burden now that I can’t work like before, and I go over every little thing—like asking my son to drive me to the doctor—as if I’ve done something wrong and should be ashamed for needing help.

S031.name: Diminished_Thinking
S031.description: Diminished ability to think or concentrate, or indecisiveness.
S031.manifestation: My mind feels slow, like it’s full of fog, so I sit there staring at the bills or my expense notebook and can’t keep the numbers straight, and even simple choices like what to eat or whether to water the plants now or later can leave me stuck for a long time.

S032.name: Death_Suicide
S032.description: Recurrent thoughts of death, recurrent suicidal ideation, or a suicide attempt.
S032.manifestation: More and more I catch myself thinking it might be easier if I just didn’t wake up one of these nights, not that I’ve planned anything, but the idea of being done with all this tiredness and worry crosses my mind a lot.
